articles.title: Contratan a un comentarista y le despiden horas después por unos mensajes en redes... de hace 14 años
articles.standfirst: Los Blazers alegan que el implicado publicó tuits "racistas y sexistas" en 2012, cuando estaba en el instituto
articles.summary: Los Blazers alegan que el implicado publicó tuits "racistas y sexistas" en 2012, cuando estaba en el instituto
articles.body: En la mañana de este jueves, los Blazers anunciaron la contratación de Braiden Bell como nuevo comentarista. Pocas horas después era despedido. La razón: unos mensajes racistas y sexistas que publicó en sus redes sociales... hace 13 años. Bell había trabajado durante dos temporadas con las Phoenix Mercury de la WNBA y había desempeñado otros cargos en el ámbito universitario. La franquicia de Portland le contrató pensando, según palabras de su presidente de operaciones comerciales, que era "la persona ideal para la dirección que estamos tomando y una voz importante para el próximo capítulo del baloncesto de los Trail Blazers". Sin embargo, a las pocas horas, la entidad emitió un comunicado anunciando el despido del trabajador más efímero en la historia del equipo. En el escrito se decía que los Blazers no podían tolerar "comentarios racistas, sexistas o dañinos", que Bell no formaría parte de la franquicia y pedían disculpas a sus aficionados. Los mensajes en cuestión son tuits de 2012 y 2013, cuando el protagonista aún estaba en el instituto. Entre otras frases se podían leer: "Los asiáticos me sacan de quicio" y "Tenemos una alerta de zorra en el pasillo 10". Bell iba a sustituir a un ilustre comentarista de los Blazers que había dejado su puesto, según él, después de haber recibido una irrisoria oferta para firmar un nuevo contrato. Es la enésima polémica que vive la franquicia con miembros de su personal desde que llegara el propietario Tom Dundon, que ya se ha ganado fama de tacaño en el universo NBA. Nada más asumir la propiedad de la franquicia despidió a cerca de 70 empleados, entre ellos a una cuarta parte de su personal de oficinas y negocio. Para ahorrar costes, a los jugadores con contrato dual se les prohibió viajar con el equipo en playoffs y también a parte del departamento de prensa y en los hoteles se acabó el privilegio de extender la hora del checkout. Para el entrenador, el presupuesto fijado era de sólo un millón de euros, lo que hizo que Tiago Splitter no aceptara la oferta y llegara Micah Nori.

Tom Dundon, propietario de los Blazers.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark's Full Box Score Stats, Top Higlights from 1st Round of WNBA Playoffs
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever are out of the 2026 WNBA Playoffs after failing to build on Caitlin Clark's season-saving Game 2 performance.
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever are out of the 2026 WNBA Playoffs after failing to build on Caitlin Clark's season-saving Game 2 performance.

Clark scored 18 points and added four assists Thursday night as the Fever conceded a 94-83 elimination loss to the Las Vegas Aces in Game 3 of the first round.

Here's a look at Clark's overall stats and top highlights from the Fever's three-game playoff run.

Clark went just 3-for-10 from deep as she was held to 15 points to open the series.

She still started out the series strong by making a few early three-pointers and splitting Aces defenders for a pass to Kelsey Mitchell while the Fever were still in contention early in the game.

Overall, the Fever struggled in Game 1 to contain the Aces, who shot 47.4 percent from behind the arc and converted 75 percent of their opportunities at the rim.

Clark made history while keeping the Fever's postseason hopes alive in Game 2.

She became the first player to record a points/assists double-double in one half of a playoff game by racking up 14 points and 11 assists through two quarters for the Fever.

Clark carried that momentum into the second half, finishing the game with a team-high 27 points to go along with 15 assists and seven rebounds.

She closed out the victory as the first player in WNBA history to record 25 points and 15 assists in a single playoff game.

The Fever successfully shut down Wilson in the final quarter of Game 2 to close out the win.

The Fever were unable to continue holding Wilson back with their season on the line.

Clark started out hot with 11 points in the first quarter to help the Fever stay even with the Aces.

She was held to just seven points in the remaining three quarters of play as Wilson racked up a game-high 36 points.

Clark also took an inadvertent elbow to the face in the fourth quarter during a play on which no foul was called.

This marks the second straight season in which Las Vegas has ended Indiana's title hopes. The Fever made it to the WNBA semifinals last season despite missing Clark to injury before losing to the Aces.

Clark finished her third WNBA regular season having averaged a career-high 22.3 points per game along with four rebounds, 8.3 assists and 1.1 steals per game. She told reporters after the Fever's elimination loss she considers this the best season of her career so far.

articles.title: Miami Heat to Celebrate Grand Theft Auto VI Release with 'A Night in Vice City' Promotion vs. Bucks
articles.summary: The Miami Heat announced Friday that they will hold a special promotional night on Nov. 18 in celebration of the release of the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI video game on Nov. 19.
articles.body:
The Miami Heat announced Friday that they will hold a special promotional night on Nov. 18 in celebration of the release of the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI video game on Nov. 19.

Entitled "A Night in Vice City," the promotion will see the Heat refer to themselves as Vice City rather than Miami for one night only when they host the Milwaukee Bucks.

The Heat will also wear brand-new uniforms and play on a never-before-seen court design.

Adding to the importance of the night is the fact that it will mark the first time Giannis Antetokounmpo plays against his old team since getting traded from the Bucks to the Heat during the offseason.

articles.title: Besiktas Istanbul - Barcelona en directo | Última hora de Euroliga en vivo hoy
articles.summary: Por aquí lo vamos dejando hoy. Ha sido un placer volver a estar aquí con vosotros, esta vez, con la victoria del Barcelona ante Besiktas. Nos vemos en
articles.body:
Última hora del Besiktas Istanbul - Barcelona

¡¡¡Muuuy buenas tardes y bienvenidos a todos y todas a la tercera jornada de la Euroliga !!! El Barcelona afronta su segunda salida consecutiva de la temporada en la cancha de Besiktas . Los de Sekulic se enfrentan al ' debutante' de la competición para intentar conseguir su primera victoria a domicilio.

Ambos equipos se encuentran empatados en la tabla, con un triunfo y una derrota, conseguidas de manera inversa. El Barcelona venció como local en su estreno ante Anadolu Efes y perdió en su visita a Dubai , mientras que Besiktas perdió en casa contra Valencia Basket y venció a domicilio contra Maccabi . Una inercia que favorece a los blaugranas para el partido de hoy.

Un partido, el del pasado martes en tierras dubaitíes , en el que Kevin Punter sostuvo al equipo con 25 puntos e hizo soñar al Barcelona con la remontada tras un desastroso segundo cuarto (29-12) . El escolta estadounidense echó en falta la aportación de alguno de sus compañeros, como los 20 puntos que anotó Brizuela el primer día contra los turcos .

En el otro lado, un Besiktas que es la única nueva cara en la Euroliga después de sustituir al Mónaco , y que tiene viejos conocidos en su plantilla. Los David DeJulius, Devon Dotson o Eugene Omoruyi , recientes jugadores de la Liga Endesa , se unen a otros que ya saben lo que es jugar en la máxima competición europea como Furkan Korkmaz, Scott Wilbekin, Wenyen Gabriel o Ante Zizic.

Desde las 19.00 horas , el Barcelona visita Estambul para buscar su primera victoria europea a domicilio y aquí estaremos para vivirlo con todos vosotros y contarlo, como siempre, en MARCA .

articles.title: Ja Morant, Damian Lillard Potentially Being Used in Bench Role Discussed by HC Ahead of NBA Season
articles.summary: With Damian Lillard set to return from injury and Ja Morant being added to the mix following an offseason trade, the Portland Trail Blazers' starting backcourt going into the 2026-27 NBA season is still being decided upon.
articles.body:
With Damian Lillard set to return from injury and Ja Morant being added to the mix following an offseason trade, the Portland Trail Blazers' starting backcourt going into the 2026-27 NBA season is still being decided upon.

Blazers head coach Micah Nori told The Athletic's Jason Quick he plans to use the preseason to tinker with the starting lineup before deciding if either Lillard or Morant will come off the bench when the regular season tips off.

Ranking Every NBA Team's Starting Lineup Ahead of Preseason 🔢

"It's not set in stone, but probably, because I'm leaning toward wanting to see what it looks like," Nori said. "And … I don't want to start a fire before I need to."

Nori's comments come after Lillard told reporters on Tuesday "as far as I know" he, Morant and Deni Avdija will all be in the starting lineup.

Lillard also said he hadn't discussed the starting five with Nori thus far. The Blazers also have Jrue Holiday as another point guard option on the roster.

According to Quick, Nori pointed out that starting Morant and Lillard "doesn't make sense" given how limited both players are defensively, which could make Holiday a more appealing option for the opening lineup.

Portland's acquisition of Morant was regarded with some confusion because of the presence of Lillard and Holiday.

B/R's Dan Favale gave the Blazers' side of the deal a "D" grade due to a combination of the players already on the team and Morant's style of play not being "particularly adaptable."

The cost to acquire Morant was so low for Portland — it only cost Jerami Grant and Kris Murray with no draft picks going back to the Memphis Grizzlies — that there's no significant risk beyond the roughly $87 million Morant is owed over the next two seasons.

Morant also offers some flexibility if Lillard is limited early in the season as he works his way back from a torn Achilles suffered on April 27, 2025. Lillard's shooting touch in practice looks to be just fine , but we have yet to see how it will play in actual games.

Our first look at the second Lillard run in Portland could come as early as Oct. 7 when the team opens preseason play against the Golden State Warriors.

articles.title: New Jalen Duren Rumors on Message from Pistons Governor That Helped Seal $200M Contract
articles.summary: Detroit Pistons owner Tom Gores reportedly played a significant role in convincing Jalen Duren to end his contract standoff by signing a five-year, $200 million deal, according to The Athletic's Sam Amick.
articles.body:
Detroit Pistons owner Tom Gores reportedly played a significant role in convincing Jalen Duren to end his contract standoff by signing a five-year, $200 million deal, according to The Athletic's Sam Amick .

According to Amick, Gores "spent Duren's decision day sending a meaningful message that played a pivotal part in his decision."

Amick reported Gores "made a promise to Duren and his family that he would help provide a more positive Pistons experience" that served as "at minimum, an acknowledgement that this sensitive situation had gone sideways."

Duren, who hit restricted free agency after averaging 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds per game in his All-Star fourth season before his production dropped in the playoffs, was eligible for a $287 million maximum contract.

Amick first reported in June Duren was considering seeking a sign-and-trade away from Detroit after being "underwhelmed" by the Pistons' first offer.

Most of the negotiations since then apparently weren't conducted directly with Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon, who said earlier this week he had "not spoken to [Duren] all summer."

The Pistons also caused friction with Duren by including mandatory monthly weight check-ins in their initial version of the $200 million offer before rescinding the clause earlier this week, Hunter Patterson and Amick reported for The Athletic.

At least some of those issues were seemingly resolved just before the restricted free agent signing deadline of Thursday night, at which point the Pistons had increased their offer from $170 to $190 million to a fully-guaranteed $200 million, per ESPN's Shams Charania .

The Pistons will now hope to bring Duren, who missed the beginning of training camp, back into the fold before tipping off the regular season Oct. 20 against the visiting Boston Celtics.

articles.title: Aces' fans spew unfounded claims that Fever fans are 'racist' while defending A'ja Wilson
articles.summary: Las Vegas Aces fans accused Indiana Fever supporters of racism and slurs at Gainbridge Fieldhouse, but their claims crumbled under scrutiny.
articles.body: There's a glaring problem in the WNBA. From media, to the players, and the league's dedicated fan base full of left-wing political activists, far too many people have been unfairly characterizing Indiana Fever and Caitlin Clark fans. Since Clark's rookie season, the claims of racism have been leveled at an astounding rate. My conversations with Las Vegas Aces' fans proved just how hostile and unfair, to say the least, that rhetoric has become. When controversies arise in the WNBA, and across sports in general, I want to do my due diligence by asking fans what they think in person. I want to hear the thoughts and opinions from people who are invested and aware in what is going on, whether they are left, right, or center. I've done that at the Sophie Cunningham rallies and protests outside arenas across the country. I've interviewed fans in the aftermath of flagrant fouls on Caitlin Clark and Cunningham. I've covered a lot of the issues the league has faced and brought upon themselves. As you know, the WNBA is no stranger to controversies. It's engrained in the fabric of the league. So when A'ja Wilson walked over 20 feet away into the seating area during Game 2 to confront a fan in Indiana for simply pointing at her from the second row of the baseline courtside seats, I wanted to hear fans thoughts about it. I wanted their thoughts on the WNBA refusing to reprimand the league's MVP or have Wilson face any repercussions whatsoever for her actions. Those questions triggered some insane accusations from Aces fans regarding the Fever fan and their fanbase. PRIME VIDEO WNBA BROADCAST CREW EMBARRASSES ITSELF WITH COVERAGE OF A'JA WILSON FAN INCIDENT About an hour before gametime, I spoke with a female Aces fan, who said, "I think it (the A'ja Wilson incident) is bigger than that moment. I think it's more about racism and the concerns regarding the Fever fans being racist." That's the way this incident was framed from the beginning, unfortunately. It was a Black athlete confronting a White fan, so people jumped at the idea there must have been a slur thrown in Wilson's direction. That was obviously not the case.She then continued by disagreeing with A'ja Wilson's actions, but justified them due to claims of racism: "She was out of line to approach a fan like that, but by the same token, racism in our country is also out of line." When I asked if she thought the fan was racist she responded, "No. Not at all." I was now a little confused, so I asked if she was claiming the fan wasn't racist, but that race played a factor in A'ja Wilson losing her cool. "I do," she said definitively. "I think as a Black athlete, in a state where there's a history of racism, and where this team has been accused of having racist fans," she continued before I cut her off to ask if there's validity to those claims. "I think there's validity to racism," she responded. "Well, of course, but [I'm asking about] Indiana Fever fans," I responded. FORMER ESPN ANCHOR SMEARS CAITLIN CLARK FANS WITH SWEEPING, FALSE ACCUSATIONS OF RACISM | MATT CALKINS "No, I can't say that," she humbly responded, realizing she was assigning labels to a fanbase without proper proof. The conversation went on for another minute or so where I respectfully pressed her on her characterization of the Fever fan base and how they've been labeled as racists, bigots, you name it. I even mentioned that Wilson even stated in the postgame interview that her actions weren't because of anything he said, but the fact that a man pointed at her. If anything, she was claiming some form of misogyny. The fan still speculated that race could've played a part in Wilson's thinking, leading her to lose her cool. In another conversation, an Aces fan unashamedly said that she believes Indiana Fever fans are "racist." She claimed, "It's (Gainbridge Fieldhouse) a hard place and the way they treat us up there. I've sat there and watched games and watched them yell slurs." When I asked her if she believed a slur was said by the fan towards Wilson, knowing good and well that no slur was stated because both I and Pat McAfee Show personality, Boston Connor, who was seated by the fan, have confirmed the fan simply said, "It (the foul) is on you," she responded by saying, "It's kinda hard to say. He did something to provoke her because that's not A'ja and that's not her demeanor." This is where I let her know that multiple sources have confirmed nothing racial was said to Wilson. "But then, the way he came [at her], he left his seat, he left his area, and he stepped towards her," she responded trying to find a way to justify Wilson's unsportsmanlike actions, though she was just proven to be ignorant about the facts. She continued by saying the Fever fan was "provoking" Wilson and seemingly questioned his intentions as a threat to Wilson's safety. Here's where things went completely off the rails. LET'S HAVE AN HONEST CONVERSATION ABOUT CAITLIN CLARK, RACISM, AND MEDIA COWARDICE| BOBBY BURACK She then claimed the WNBA made the right decision to not eject, fine, or suspend Wilson, because Indiana Fever fans are "racists." I'm not kidding. This was actually her argument. "If you've never been to Cambridge Fieldhouse and seen the demeanor of the Indiana Fever fans," she mistakenly said while referring to Gainbridge Fieldhouse. "If we did half of what they did up there, the WNBA would be fining the Aces." So now was the time to get the clarification we are all looking for. I asked, "Do you believe Indiana Fever fans are racist?" She responded with a resounding, "Yes! By all means! By all means! By all means! Yes, they are racists." So here is the problem. Fans like this, making outlandish claims that aren't based in facts or reality, are what is wrong with the WNBA. They spew unfounded talking points about Fever fans. It's been that way since Clark entered the league three seasons ago. The millions of people who have flocked to the league because of Caitlin Clark, helping players like A'ja Wilson sign million dollar contracts, assisted in teams now flying private, and who may be the fans who help make the league profitable for the first time in the league's 30-year history, are labeled as the scum of the earth. They might as well be considered the KKK of WNBA fanbases. An insane, divisive, unfair label that echoes the claims of even A'ja Wilson's mom, who paraded around the arena with a "Love Beats Hate" sign following the Aces' Game 3 win. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Also, these accusations and rhetoric only devalues legitimate racism. There is still racism in America, and it's not just White people discriminating against Blacks, but we have to stop making claims like this, if they can't be substantiated. All you're doing is insulting your paying customers and fellow fans in the most vile way.

articles.title: NBA reportedly won't discipline Wizards, Bub Carrington after guard admitted team held back to get AJ Dybantsa
articles.summary: The Wizards recorded only 17 victories in 2025-26 — their second-fewest in single-season franchise history — before winning the No. 1 overall pick and drafti...
articles.body:
The NBA cracked down on purposeful losing, otherwise known as "tanking," last season. Back in February, the league fined the Utah Jazz $500,000 and the Indiana Pacers $100,000 for fishy roster-management behavior that NBA commissioner Adam Silver described as "overt" in its prioritization of draft position over winning.

Then, in May, the league announced its new anti-tanking rules , which will be in place for at least the 2027-29 drafts. The draft lottery will grow from 14 to 16 teams. Lottery odds will be flattened further. And, most notably, the teams with the three worst records will be penalized .

But as much as the NBA is trying to eliminate tanking, it's reportedly letting an admission of the integrity-threatening practice slide ahead of the 2026-27 campaign. Washington Wizards guard Bub Carrington, a 21-year-old gearing up for his third season with the organization, confessed that the Wizards didn't give their all last season. Yet, according to a Friday report from The Athletic's Sam Amick , the NBA won't discipline Washington or Carrington.

"We just haven't been told yet to go be the best version of yourself," Carrington said in a now-viral clip from a 1-on-1 interview with Washington TV station WUSA9.

Carrington was asked to clarify what he meant.

"We've all, in a way, been held back. Just because … we were trying to get AJ Dybantsa."

Carrington continued before letting out a laugh: "That's no secret."

He repeated those three words again before adding, "But now, no one has handcuffs. Everyone's shackles-free. So that alone is already a conversation starter. But then you put that on top of the coaching, on top of the vets that we have — that's a playoff team.

"And that's gonna happen. … And then when it does happen, it'll happen for a long time."

Really, what's been a conversation starter is Carrington's candor. His remarks were only surprising because he actually said what everyone was thinking.

The Wizards recorded only 17 victories in 2025-26 — their second-fewest in single-season franchise history — before winning the No. 1 overall pick and drafting Dybantsa.

They were among a handful of teams, a group that included the Jazz and the Pacers, not so discretely jockeying for draft positioning last season, after which a talent-laden class of NBA prospects were available for the taking.

Dybantsa, a standout forward who averaged a nation-leading 25.5 points in his lone season at BYU, headlined that cohort.

The Wizards, who haven't won more than 18 games in each of the past three go-arounds, traded for four-time All-Star guard Trae Young and 10-time All-Star big man Anthony Davis during last season. But Washington didn't hurry them back from the injuries they had suffered with the Atlanta Hawks and Dallas Mavericks, respectively. Young wound up appearing in only five games with the Wizards, and Davis has yet to play in a contest with Washington.

Not only that, but the Wizards gave plenty of minutes to players who had spent time with their G League team, including those on two-way contracts.

With Young and Davis in the rotation, plus a young corps surrounding them, the Wizards could be one of the most improved teams in the NBA this season. They also might be one of the last beneficiaries of tanking as we knew it.

articles.title: Far-left ESPN writer mocks Caitlin Clark for losing in the WNBA playoffs, says it proves she isn't a top gurad
articles.summary: ESPN race writer David Dennis Jr. openly celebrated Caitlin Clark's WNBA playoff elimination, posting a smiling photo and calling her overrated.
articles.body: An ESPN writer openly celebrated Caitlin Clark's elimination from the WNBA playoffs on Friday by posting a smiling photo of himself on X. David Dennis Jr. then posted a lengthy thread mocking Clark as overrated. Dennis referenced his previous argument that Clark is "not a top four guard" in the WNBA and claimed this postseason proved him right. "But let the record reflect that I was 100% right here as well. Because yes we did talk about winning and my concerns about her game translating to winning," Dennis wrote. He then gloated over Clark losing in the first round. "A team with 3 top 10 players, according to ESPN, who was a game away from the Finals w/o their star player and then getting bounced in the first round w/ said player is a reason to ask questions. It always is." ESPN'S COVERAGE OF CAITLIN CLARK IS A RACIALLY CHARGED, DISHONEST, AND EMBARRASSING MESS | BOBBY BURACK For context, the Fever lost to the Las Vegas Aces, the heavy betting favorites to win their fourth championship in five years. Framing that as Clark getting "bounced in the first round" is intentionally more dismissive than descriptive. Clark also played well. She became the first player in WNBA history to score 25+ and 15 assists in any game. She is not the reason the Fever lost to a superior team. Those unfamiliar with Dennis might reasonably wonder why an employee of ESPN, the WNBA Finals rights holder, would celebrate the elimination of the league's biggest television draw. Imagine an NBC personality gloating over the Chiefs' or Cowboys' playoff exit in a season in which NBC broadcasts the Super Bowl. We can explain. David Dennis Jr. is a hack. This is the same commentator who last year called for Caitlin Clark fans — who represent a significant portion of the WNBA's audience — to stop watching the league. ESPN hired Dennis in 2021, promoting that it had "hired the son of a civil rights leader." His addition was part of the network's post-George Floyd hiring push, during which ESPN publicly emphasized race and representation in its talent strategy. ESPN WRITER WHO BLAMED RACISM FOR HIS ARREST SAYS RACISM IS NOT TO BLAME FOR CAITLIN CLARK HATE Dennis is a DEI hire, by definition. And he tries far too hard. Last year, he posted a rant on Bluesky claiming Sydney Sweeney's American Eagle jeans advertisement "mortified" him because he believed it promoted eugenics. Dennis seems to have an issue with successful White women, whether it's Clark, Sweeney, or Sophie Cunningham. He is running the same playbook that Jemele Hill, Bomani Jones, and Ryan Clark used before him. Clark's firing, followed by his unfounded accusations of racism against the network, will likely keep Dennis employed for a few more years. But he's drifting into the sort of territory where only Dan Le Batard would offer him a job. Speaking of Le Batard, one of his employees, Jessica Smetana, also celebrated the Fever's loss. She compared watching Sophie Cunningham play basketball to serving a sentence at Shawshank. Like Dennis, Smetana comes across as so bitter. She is probably jealous of Cunningham, as well. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP And yet, these same commentators who proudly belittle Clark and Cunningham continue to claim that Black lesbian women are the ones the sports media relentlessly targets. It's all such a lie.

articles.title: Un sólido Barça muestra su poderío ante un Besiktas caótico
articles.standfirst: Punter (16) y Gibson (15) comandan el convincente triunfo azulgrana en Estambul
articles.summary: Punter (16) y Gibson (15) comandan el convincente triunfo azulgrana en Estambul
articles.body: Un Barça tremendamente sólido, aguerrido en defensa y muy acertado desde el triple (9/21) desarboló con relativa facilidad a un Besiktas caótico y demasiado individualista (82-95). La gran defensa azulgrana sumió a los turcos en un desorden y una inoperancia preocupantes que les llevó a jugarse la baza de los triples en vano (8/33). Punter (16) y Gibson (15) fueron los mejores de los de Sekulic. Mientras que Wilbekin (17) y Zizic (10+9) destacaron entre los locales, que evitaron una paliza mayor gracias a sus 18 rebotes ofensivos, el único lunar culé en Estambul. Dotson lideró las primeras embestidas del Besiktas (6-2), una efervescencia que fue diluida pronto por la eficaz telaraña defensiva de un Barça muy proactivo que con un parcial de 2-18 fabricado con puntos de ocho jugadores diferentes y coronado con triples de Umude y Martin puso la máxima en el marcador (8-20, min 8). Wilbekin, con cinco puntos, comandó la reacción de los turcos, muy erráticos en los tiros (3/13 t2 y 2/9 t3), pero que sacaban petróleo de sus siete rebotes ofensivos (17-25, min 10). El resurgimiento del Besiktas continuó al inico del segundo acto con Wilbekin, Dotson y Gabriel completando un parcial de 14-5 (24-27, min 14). No hubo sorpasso porque los azulgranas cortaron esa inercia con los triples de Minaya, Punter y Brizuela que devolvieron la máxima a los suyos (31-43, min 16). Brown y Nowell frenaron la sangría, aunque Brizuela, Parra y Gibson continuaron percutiendo en el aro turco para mantener la renta al descanso (40-52, min 20). No cejó el Barça en su empeño de estiran su ventaja y en la reanudación lo hizo con autoridad gracias a Balcerowski, Gibson y Nkamohua, que pusieron una nueva máxima (49-63, min 25). Los turcos, muy individualistas, se estrellaban una y otra vez contra el muro defensivo azulgrana y en defensa eran taladrados por sus tiradores. Wilbekin y Zizic les sacaron por momentos de la UVI, a la que regresaron heridos por el acierto de Robinson, Martin, Umude y Gibson (62-77, min 30). El Besiktas se suicidó desde el triple con un deplorable 5/25 que le hundió más aún en el fango. Todo lo contrario que el Barça, muy entonado desde el perímetro (8/18). Gibson y Balcerowski pusieron una máxima renta (64-81, min 33) que ya resultó inalcanzable para los turcos. Los deslavazados intentos de Morgan, Korkmaz y Zizic por aliviar el caos de los suyos (73-83, min 35) fueron contrarrestados por dos canastas de Punter, máximo anotador de un Barça sólido y muy superior (82-95). 82 - Besiktas (17+23+22+20): Dotson (11), Morgan (8), Brown (17), Nowell (6), Zizic (10) -cinco inicial- DeJulius (2), Ugurlu (-), Birsen (6), Wilbekin (4), Omoruyi (2), Korkmaz (6) y Gabriel (10). 95 - Barça (25+27+25+18): Punter (16), Robinson (9), Balcerowski (11), Minaya (5), Parra (7) -cinco inicial- Gibson (15), Martin (7), Umude (6), Brizuela (8), Nkamhoua (-) y Núñez (11). Árbitros: Borys Ryzhyk, Michele Rossi y Anne Panther. Sin eliminados. Incidencias: partido correspondiente a la tercera jornada de la Euroliga disputado en el pabellón Turkcell Basketbol Gelişim Merkezi de Estambul.
